The agent's internal predictive model developed null structure in its planner, from which the Minkowski causal structure was reconstructed with high accuracy.

entry.title: Failure odds of quantum hashing when some seeds are bad
entry.summary: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies hashing used to extract secure randomness against quantum adversaries, as in quantum random number generation and key distribution. It bounds the probability of failure in practical settings where a seed may be reused across rounds and may not be ideal. The authors show that randomness extraction against quantum side information yields near-uniform random numbers except with a bounded failure probability. They extend this guarantee to blockwise hashing over multiple rounds and relax the almost two-universality assumption.

entry.title: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform
entry.summary: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Qyantram, an open quantum computing platform with four subsystems: a staged compilation pipeline, a router, an error identification engine, and a machine-learning engine. Its verification exploits inactive qubits remaining in the |0> state, reducing complexity from 2^N to 2^k and achieving about 10,000x speed-ups on 127- and 156-qubit layouts. The router publishes rejected SWAP candidates and their scores, but introduces about 1.27x more SWAP gates than Qiskit's SABRE.

entry.title: Belief-propagation-guided Tesseract decoding for quantum LDPC codes
entry.summary: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a faster version of the Tesseract decoder, a search-based method for quantum error correction. Damped belief propagation is run before the search, and its hard decision is accepted directly when it matches the triggered detectors, skipping the search. Otherwise, BP marginal estimates adjust the search priority. Evaluated on bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise, the method reduces expanded search nodes by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates while keeping the logical error rate close to Tesseract's.

entry.title: Explicit lossless expanders and good quantum codes with full-rank checks.
entry.summary: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper constructs explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank. Using a free action of a finite 2-group, it obtains asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness. The construction also yields Ramanujan Cayley graphs on 2-groups by reducing LPS Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2. Applied within the Hong, Guo, and Lucas framework, the codes give quantum memories with improved guaranteed lifetime.

entry.title: AI scientists reimagining computational quantum research, a study on automating the reproduction of quantum papers.
entry.summary: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces OmniQ, an expert-audited environment that turns 59 published computational quantum studies into executable reproduction tasks. It finds that current AI scientist systems often fail to reproduce published results, while human expert input can turn these failures into successful reproductions. The authors present Residual Agents, a self-improving system that stores verified workflow repairs, and integrate the reproduced results into a platform built on the model context protocol.

entry.title: Whether and how fast the regularized quantum channel relative entropy can be computed
entry.summary: Finite attainment and efficient computation of regularized quantum channel relative entropy arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies when the regularized quantum channel relative entropy is attained at finite blocklength and how efficiently it can be approximated. It shows a dichotomy: the value is either attained at the single-copy level or never attained at any finite blocklength, and a simple two-copy additivity test distinguishes the two cases. The authors also give explicit convergence rates for approximating the regularized value and a semidefinite hierarchy yielding a certified polynomial-time approximation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish a dichotomy for finite attainment of regularized channel relative entropy, a two-copy additivity test, and explicit convergence rates.

entry.title: Quantum state synthesis using an NP oracle
entry.summary: State Synthesis with an NP oracle arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This note presents a quantum algorithm that prepares an arbitrary state to inverse exponential precision in polynomial time using queries to an NP oracle, assuming direct access to entries of the state vector. The previous best upper bound on the required oracle complexity class was PP. The paper shows that any quantum algorithm with a P/poly oracle needs exponentially many queries, suggesting NP is the best possible upper bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the oracle complexity upper bound for arbitrary state preparation from PP to NP, and report an exponential query lower bound for P/poly oracles.

entry.title: MBUndo: Automatic, Sound, Efficient Measurement-Based Uncomputation for Quantum Circuits
entry.summary: MBUndo: Sound, Automatic, and Efficient Measurement-Based Uncomputation for Quantum Circuits arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses how quantum programs reset temporary ancilla qubits to zero, a step called uncomputation. It replaces costly unitary T gates with cheaper measurements and phase corrections, a technique called measurement-based uncomputation. The authors present a static analysis that finds where measurement is safe for each ancilla and circuit transformations that convert unitary uncomputation gates into phase corrections. Their compiler pass MBUndo reduces T gates by more than 36.5% across 22 benchmarks compared with existing uncomputation synthesizers.

entry.title: Achieving CSS code limits over Pauli channels with bounded graphical complexity
entry.summary: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper constructs ensembles of Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum codes whose rates approach the CSS limit over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding, while keeping sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The approach separates parity-check density from graphical complexity by representing dense components through sparse concatenated factor graphs. The authors first analyze LDPC and LDGM component code combinations numerically, then introduce a second construction using concatenated LDPC, LDGM, and GIRA codes. They use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct concatenated LDPC, LDGM and GIRA CSS ensembles that approach the hashing bound with bounded graphical complexity.

entry.title: Qubrio: Faster, More Accurate Quantum Compilation Using Teams of AI Agents
entry.summary: Qubrio: High-Performance Quantum Compilation via Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents Qubrio, a framework that uses multiple large language model agents to compile quantum programs, reducing the need for manual redesign of compiler rules when hardware changes. It splits programs into sequential stages and assigns specialized agents to placement, routing, and optimization, with feedback used for error correction. On realistic workloads, it improves hardware runtime and program fidelity over the state-of-the-art PowerMove compiler, and its code is publicly available.

entry.title: "Seeing Why": Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
entry.summary: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces Born evidence maps, which exactly split each class probability of quantum and all-optical image classifiers into contributions from the encoded image amplitudes. In simulation, four phase plates reach 72.3% accuracy on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston hardware, 300 Caltech-10 test pictures were classified at 37.7% accuracy, against 10% by chance. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact evidence decomposition for linear quantum and optical classifiers, equal to Integrated Gradients, and report hardware validation on IBM's ibm_kingston.

entry.title: Tensor contraction using ZX calculus and graph-based rewriting
entry.summary: Tensor Contraction with ZX Calculus, a Graph-Theoretic Approach arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper studies tensor contraction, the evaluation of tensor networks, which is widely used in computer science, physics, and applied mathematics. Finding an optimal bond-by-bond contraction order is NP-hard, so the author proposes first applying graph-theoretic rewrite preprocessing to obtain an equivalent network whose line graph has lower treewidth. The rewriting focuses on ZX calculus, a diagrammatic language for quantum circuits. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

entry.title: Long-term bond yields computed as quantum ground-state energies using a single-setting VQE on two NISQ devices
entry.summary: Long-term yields of short-rate models as Feynman-Kac ground states: a variational quantum eigensolver with single-setting energy estimation on two NISQ platforms arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper shows that the long-term yield of a short-rate model equals the ground-state energy of a Schrödinger operator derived from the Feynman-Kac bond-pricing equation, enabling computation by a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). It covers the Vasicek, CIR and Black-Karasinski models, calibrated monthly to the U.S. Treasury curve from 1985 to 2026. On the ibm_cleveland and IonQ Forte Enterprise devices, the single-setting energy estimator yields errors about ten times smaller than a Pauli-measurement VQE on the same circuits.

entry.title: Quantum lower bounds for finding and testing k-to-one collisions in strings
entry.summary: Quantum Lower Bounds for Collision Problems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper studies quantum query complexity for Promised k-to-one Finding on an exactly k-to-one string over a fixed alphabet. It gives tight lower bounds for both adaptive algorithms and one-round non-adaptive algorithms, the latter matching classical birthday sampling even with entangled queries. It also proves a non-adaptive lower bound for k-to-one Testing, resolving an open question from Koiran, Landes, Portier, and Yao. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight quantum lower bounds for k-to-one collision problems and resolve an open question of Koiran et al., via compressed permutation oracles.

entry.title: OptiPESS: a GPU-accelerated framework that adaptively allocates resources for quantum-chemistry PES scans
entry.summary: A GPU-Accelerated and Geometry-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Optimized PES Scans with CUDA-Q arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper addresses batched VQE and QAOA potential energy surface scans, where many Hamiltonians differ only in coefficients. It proposes OptiPESS, a GPU-accelerated runtime that uses a Locality-Occupancy-Variance metric to measure Hamiltonian similarity and schedule iteration and shot budgets adaptively. Implemented on CUDA-Q, the authors report reductions of up to 78.3% in evaluations and 74.8% in wall-time while maintaining baseline accuracy.

entry.title: Hidden selection rules and amplitude ceilings in quantum Fourier models
entry.summary: Hidden selection rules and amplitude ceilings in quantum Fourier models arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies quantum models with Pauli data encodings, which compute trigonometric polynomials whose expressivity depends on the Fourier coefficients a circuit can reach. It identifies two structural rules that can be checked before training: an antiunitary time-reversal rule and a unitary reflection rule, which remove certain frequencies. For gate-level circuits, deciding whether such a rule exists reduces to a linear system over GF(2) solvable in polynomial time, and the time-reversal rule holds in 17.6% of 6,120 standard template configurations. The paper also derives a tight ceiling of 2^(-m) on the top coefficient for single-upload encodings and a depth-independent bound for re-uploading, which were not violated on a non-linearity benchmark and predicted trained performance on real data, with experiments on a 65-qubit IBM chain.

entry.title: Benchmark of quantum statevector simulators for scientific computing
entry.summary: Benchmark Study for Quantum Statevector Simulators for Scientific Computing arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper benchmarks three open-source quantum simulators, Cirq (qsim), CUDA-Q, and Qiskit (Aer), on a single Azure virtual machine. The test simulates the 2D quantum acoustic wave equation for 7 to 29 qubits, measuring CPU and GPU runtime, multi-core scalability, and GPU-over-CPU speedup. The rankings differ across categories, and no single framework dominates in all configurations. The authors conclude that backend choice should depend on hardware and problem size.

entry.title: Keeping quantum bias: pushforward repair for constrained quantum optimization.
entry.summary: Leaving Quantum Bias on the Table: Pushforwards as a Path to Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper addresses constrained quantum samplers that often output infeasible solutions, proposing a post-measurement framework that maps the raw quantum sampling distribution onto the feasible set using classical feasibility maps built from constraint-violation statistics. Each repaired solution's probability equals the total raw mass of its repair preimage. For permutation constraints it uses Hungarian maximum-overlap repair with O(n^3) cost. On traveling-salesman instances, a 10-city case recovered the optimum with about 10^3 shots versus 10^6 in the original CE-QAOA workflow, and on a 127-qubit IBM processor repaired candidates matched reference tours on smaller benchmarks and improved them on larger ones.

entry.title: Discovering Physical Models for Experimental Quantum Systems Using Agentic AI
entry.summary: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces an AI-driven model discovery framework in which a large language model agent, using tools and a structured workflow, proposes candidate Hamiltonian and Lindbladian models, generates computational tools, and quantitatively evaluates competing physical hypotheses. The workflow is applied to three previously published cavity-QED datasets from color centers in diamond and silicon carbide. The agent identifies physical models for these systems and characterizes disorder among emitters.

entry.title: Quantized scar multiplets and dissipative cat states in an open quantum baker map
entry.summary: Fractal Period Locking and Action-Quantized Resonances in the Open Quantum Baker Map arXiv · Oct 16, 2026The paper studies an open quantum baker map with a position window of width w centered at q_c. Classical pruning divides the (q_c, w) plane into diamond-shaped regions where the leading resonances form root-of-unity multiplets. At w = 1/2, one periodic orbit survives for almost every q_c, and the multiplets have modulus 2^{-1/2} with phase equal to the orbit action.

entry.title: Single-shot state preparation threshold: a rigorous theorem and statistical mechanical mapping
entry.summary: Single-shot state preparation thresholds in quantum LDPC codes: soundness, confinement, and statistical mechanics arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper studies the threshold for preparing logical codewords using one round of noisy syndrome measurements, called single-shot state preparation. The authors prove that for CSS quantum LDPC codes with at least logarithmic distance, linear confinement alone guarantees a nonzero threshold, and under linear soundness the residual data error is local stochastic. They also develop a statistical mechanical mapping expressing the logical error rate as a partition function, and Monte Carlo simulations on the three-dimensional toric code suggest sublinear soundness can also support the threshold. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove linear confinement alone yields a single-shot preparation threshold for CSS qLDPC codes, without soundness, and report Monte Carlo results on the 3D toric code suggesting sublinear s

entry.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones, with a five-party gap and dependence on local dimension
entry.summary: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper studies the linear inequalities that entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy, focusing on the entropy vectors achievable by stabilizer states, which underpin quantum error correction. After a linear lift, the closure of this cone is shown to be exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object with one more element than there are parties, built from rank functions of subspace arrangements over GF(d). For five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, witnessed by an explicit six-variable inequality. The cone also depends on the local dimension, and for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone for every odd local dimension.

entry.title: Beyond Light Cones: Complexity of Preparing States for Quantum Spin Glasses
entry.summary: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper introduces a method for studying how hard it is to prepare states of dense quantum p-spin Hamiltonians, going beyond limits based only on circuit light cones. It uses an effective profile complexity derived from Pauli profiles. The authors show that near-ground-state energy requires Ω(n²/log n) one- and two-qubit gates, and they give depth-width, entanglement and matrix product state lower bounds. ★★★★ Notable: Combines a nonsymmetric quantum de Finetti theorem with Gaussian process entropy bounds to go beyond lightcone limits, reporting Omega(n^2/log n) gate lower bounds and magic-hierarchy obstructions.

entry.title: A Tale of Two Walks: Linking Kac's Quantum Random Walk to the KMP Process
entry.summary: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper shows that the parallel Kac walk's twirling channel on the symmetric subspace is exactly encoded by a classical Markov chain on partitions, which lifts to a parallel KMP process on complete graphs. The authors prove that O(log d + log(1/ε)) repetitions approximate Haar twirling to error ε, uniformly in the number of copies t. They also give a mixing-time bound for standard KMP on general graphs and apply it to improve coordinate hit-and-run mixing on the simplex. ★★★★ Notable: Reveals a new link between parallel Kac walk and KMP; the authors report Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace approximated in repetitions independent of t, and improve simplex coordinate hit-and-ru

entry.title: Scalable Coherent-Noise Tomography Using Stabilizer-Code Polarization
entry.summary: Probing Coherent Noise with Stabilizer Codes: Identifiability, Ambiguity, and Decoder Priors arXiv · Oct 14, 2026The paper proposes a constant-cost method for characterizing coherent noise in quantum error correction, which is hard to detect with standard Pauli-twirl techniques. Measurement-free error correction projects few-qubit coherent noise onto a single-logical-qubit effective channel, and a concatenated fingerprint built from bit-flip and phase-flip codes is shown to uniquely recover the noise parameters. A synthetic numerical test over 500 sampled parameter points found full-rank Jacobians, supporting first-order identifiability. The authors expect the recovered model to lower logical error rates for surface-code decoders, but this is an anticipated benefit rather than a demonstrated result.

entry.title: Early fault-tolerant magic state generation using color codes on a superconducting processor
entry.summary: Early Fault-Tolerant Magic State Synthesis and Spacetime Efficient Analog Rotations with Color Code on a Superconducting Quantum Processor arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper reports the first implementations of two magic state generation methods on a superconducting quantum processor using the color code: STAR for near-term computing and fault-tolerant magic state synthesis for long-term computing. The authors present a STAR-type injection protocol on the color code and build an MSS factory from multi-patch magic state cultivation, interleaved transversal Clifford operations, and lattice-surgery teleportation. Fidelity results under post-selection are reported, and post-selection, most-likely-error, and concatenated-matching decoding are compared. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first superconducting-processor implementations of STAR injection and multi-patch cultivation on the color code, reaching about 91% logical magic state fidelity.

entry.title: Triple descent in quantum linear regression
entry.summary: Triple descent in quantum linear regression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies prediction error in quantum linear regression models, such as quantum extreme learning machines and quantum fidelity kernels, when features are estimated from finitely many measurement shots. As the number of measurement outcomes grows, the error shows a triple-descent profile with two peaks of different origins. A classical peak arises when the measurement first becomes informationally complete and can be suppressed by more shots at inference. A quantum peak appears when outcomes match training states and cannot be removed by more shots. Using random-matrix theory, the authors derive both peak shapes analytically, including ridge regularization. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a second, quantum peak from finite-shot noise in quantum linear regression, derived analytically via random-matrix theory including ridge regularization.

entry.title: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification for symmetric Werner states
entry.summary: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper exactly computes the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification for normalized symmetric Werner states in every local dimension d≥2, giving a closed-form expression. The authors prove additivity for tensor powers and for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. They show that the canonical purification and its products achieve these values even when arbitrary joint purifications with finite-dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. The paper also proves continuity of the optimal value at the symmetric endpoint under perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an exact closed form for the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of symmetric Werner states, with additivity and global optimality results.

entry.title: Checking the five-electron pO silicon qubit with full configuration interaction
entry.summary: Validation of the five-electron pO qubit in Si using full configuration interaction arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines a recently proposed charge qubit, pO, made of five electrons in a gate-defined silicon quantum dot. The authors use full configuration interaction calculations to test how Coulomb interactions affect whether this qubit is viable. They find that the interacting states occupy orbital shells beyond the simple shell-filling picture. For valley splittings above about 50 μeV, the qubit still has zero dipole moment and a nonzero quadrupole tensor.

entry.title: Three-photon EIT and absorption in room-temperature Rb vapor using two collinear beam cascades
entry.summary: ⁸⁵Rb electromagnetically induced transparency and absorption on two collinear 5S₁/2→5P₁/2→5D₃/2→ 25F₅/2 three-photon cascade schemes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This study examines electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature ⁸⁵Rb vapor, using a three-photon cascade through the 5S₁/₂, 5P₁/₂, 5D₃/₂ and 25F₅/₂ levels. Two collinear laser-beam configurations are tested while the detunings of the upper two lasers are varied, producing rich transmission features. The authors explain the spectra with a dressed-atom model and a quantum Monte Carlo trajectory method. Measurements in cells containing 50 and 500 mTorr of argon gas are also used to study collisional effects.

entry.title: Zero-mode-free detector coupling via spatial derivatives
entry.summary: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Particle detector models in cavity QED often omit zero modes or assume their state, which can compromise causality or make predictions ambiguous. This paper shows that spatial-derivative coupling removes both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively.

entry.title: Applying a quantum machine learning algorithm to predicting server thermal behavior
entry.summary: Application a quantum machine learning algorithm to the applied problem of modeling the thermal regime of a servers arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether quantum machine learning can be applied to a real-world problem. The researchers trained a quantum circuit to predict the temperature of eight GPUs in each node of a high-performance computing cluster, using 16 physical parameters. The quantum approach performed as well as classical machine learning on this task. Using model problems, the authors also showed that quantum machine learning could potentially outperform classical methods.

entry.title: Phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave packets in the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator
entry.summary: Phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures in the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures in the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator, which models a Kerr medium. From the time-evolved state, the authors derive analytical expressions for the Dunkl-Husimi Q-function and a normalized angular Husimi profile. The Dunkl parameter changes coherent-state excitation weights and parity-dependent phase accumulation, producing angular anisotropy and asymmetric phase-space separation. For μ=0.5 asymmetric multicomponent patterns with unequal peak heights appear, reconstructing early at t=π/λ, while for μ=1.0 the distribution broadens but stays multimodal. The standard Kerr dynamics are recovered as μ→0.

entry.title: Mirror performance of a two-colour optical cavity under blue and red light in vacuum
entry.summary: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This study examines how a vacuum optical cavity with high-reflectivity coatings at 455 nm and 671 nm changes over time under high circulating power. After 11 hours of continuous exposure, the 455 nm finesse dropped from 7.7×10³ to 1.9×10³, while the 671 nm finesse showed no measurable degradation. The authors also report partial recovery of the 455 nm finesse when the cavity is illuminated at 455 nm in air.

entry.title: Benchmarking quantum neural networks and classical stand-ins on long-range correlated quantum models
entry.summary: Benchmarking Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks and their classical surrogates on long-range strongly correlated models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper compares quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) with their classical surrogates for distinguishing phases in one-dimensional strongly correlated systems that include interactions beyond nearest neighbours. It uses an anisotropic Heisenberg spin chain and an extended t-t' Fermi-Hubbard model as test cases, training classifiers on labelled ground-state data to map finite-size phase diagrams. The authors also apply Pauli backpropagation and study how truncation parameters trade off approximation accuracy against the size of the resulting Pauli expansion.

entry.title: Distance to integrability and complexity
entry.summary: Distance to integrability and complexity arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies nearest-neighbour interactions on spin-1/2 chains. It identifies the full set of integrable models of this form and uses a numerical algorithm to find the closest integrable model for a given Hamiltonian, defining a model-independent distance to integrability. Standard chaos measures are shown to interpolate between integrable and chaotic values as this distance increases. However, values vary widely across models, and the distance provides information not directly given by these diagnostics.

entry.title: Quantum Simulation of Hadronization: From String Breaking to Event Generation
entry.summary: Quantum Simulation of Hadronization: From String Breaking to Event Generation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026High-energy collisions produce quarks and gluons that QCD binds into hadrons, a real-time, non-perturbative process. Current event generators use phenomenological models fitted to data, and their uncertainties limit some Large Hadron Collider measurements. This white paper summarizes a workshop and proposes a roadmap for extending existing quantum simulations of string breaking to inform these models. It outlines toy models, observables to extract, and challenges, and a staged program in which quantum simulations first qualitatively and later quantitatively improve event generators.

entry.title: Complete construction of generalized parent Hamiltonians for matrix product states
entry.summary: Exhaustive Construction of Generalized Parent Hamiltonians for Matrix Product States arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to build local Hamiltonians that have a given translation-invariant matrix product state (MPS) as an eigenstate. Beyond the standard frustration-free parent Hamiltonians, it allows non-Hermitian telescoping terms that cancel under periodic boundary conditions, yielding an exhaustive construction. The authors relate inequivalent classes of these Hamiltonians to the spectrum of the MPS transfer matrix, discuss properties such as non-Abelian symmetries and zero correlation length, and extend the framework to block-injective MPS.

entry.title: Simulating real-time Yukawa particle dynamics on qubit-qumode quantum hardware
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of real-time Yukawa dynamics with qubits and qumodes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes simulating particle scattering in the (1+1)-dimensional Yukawa theory on a hybrid qubit-qumode device, with fermions on qubits and the scalar field on oscillators. The authors emulate this device with tensor networks to study single-scalar decay and fermion-antifermion scattering near resonance. They compare the results with lattice perturbation theory and find that the emulation resolves corrections beyond the Dyson summation of the one-loop self-energy.

entry.title: Heavy quarkonium dynamics beyond binding-energy-over-temperature expansion
entry.summary: Heavy quarkonium dynamics beyond the binding energy over temperature expansion arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper revisits the pNRQCD open-quantum-system description of bottomonium in a quark-gluon plasma, deriving the full master equation in a spherical basis. The equation avoids an expansion in the binding energy over temperature and is simulated as a positive-sector Lindblad equation using the open-source code QTraj. The authors compute in-medium widths and Bjorken-evolved survival probabilities for the Υ(1S, 2S, 3S) states, showing convergence of the expansion at high temperatures and providing first large-scale quantum-trajectory results at low temperatures.

entry.title: Controlling measurement angles to purify a continuously monitored quantum oscillator
entry.summary: Measurement-angle control of a continuously monitored quantum oscillator: purification limits and optimal protocols arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies a quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a thermal bath and continuously monitored by up to two detectors, where the control variable is each detector's quadrature measurement angle. Within the Gaussian regime, the conditional covariance follows a deterministic Riccati equation. The authors propose and compare constant-rate, greedy, vibrational, and variational monitoring strategies by the purity they sustain, relative to lab-fixed or phase-locked detectors. They also analyze how breaking measurement-frame anisotropy causes these strategies' performance to diverge.

entry.title: A New Non-Affine Family in the Karlsson–Szöllősi Intersection of Complex Hadamard Matrices
entry.summary: Classification of the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection arXiv · Oct 24, 2026The paper shows that, up to standard Hadamard equivalence, the intersection of Karlsson's K_6^{(2)} and Szöllősi's X_6^{(2)} two-parameter families equals the known affine Diţă curve D_6^{(1)} together with a new non-affine one-parameter family C_6^{(1)}. The authors give a new parametrisation of X_6^{(2)} in Karlsson coordinates and a constructive classification of the intersection. They suggest this may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a new non-affine one-parameter family C6(1) in the Karlsson-Szöllősi intersection, showing it is strictly larger than the known affine curve D6(1), with a constructive classificatio

entry.title: Fastest quantum evolution under fixed-norm generators
entry.summary: Time-optimal quantum dynamics under fixed-norm generators arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies quantum systems whose evolution is driven by linear generators with a fixed unitarily invariant norm. For this class, it derives a universal time-optimal generator that converts one given state into another, yielding a time-optimal non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for pure-state conversion. The general result is then used to obtain quantum speed limits for mixed-state evolutions governed by Lindbladians and non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a universal time-optimal generator and quantum speed limits under fixed unitarily invariant norms, using GL(n,C) geodesic geometry for arbitrary dimension and mixed states.

entry.title: Which gaps survive in the unitary almost Mathieu operator, and which close
entry.summary: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps Ten Dry Martinis, Five on the Rim arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper determines exactly which gap labels correspond to open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants in (0,1]. When both couplings are below one, every permitted gap label is open, including the critical case where the couplings are equal. When at least one coupling equals one, both lifts of odd winding labels are open, while all even winding labels collapse. ★★★★ Notable: The authors exactly characterize which gap labels are open for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at all irrational frequencies and couplings, including the critical case.

entry.title: Functional tensor train methods for high-order Greeks and exposure tails of multi-asset structured products
entry.summary: Functional Tensor Trains for High-Order Greeks and Exposure Tails of Multi-Asset Structured Products arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes solving the backward pricing recursion for worst-of autocallable notes using a piecewise-polynomial functional tensor train (hp-FTT), so that one solve yields all Greeks at any spot and the potential future exposure quantile without Monte Carlo sampling noise. Comparing against strong Monte Carlo estimators on worst-of autocallables observed monthly on three to five assets, the authors find Monte Carlo cheaper for first-order Greeks at 1% accuracy, while hp-FTT is cheaper for third-order Greeks at that accuracy and for all checked Greeks at 0.1%. The results depend on derivative order, accuracy target, and number of assets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors solve the backward pricing recursion with piecewise-polynomial tensor trains split at barriers, obtaining all Greeks in one solve, and report cost comparisons against Monte Carlo on three

entry.title: Proof that the quartic gap between quantum and dequantized linear algebra algorithms is tight
entry.summary: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies quantum linear algebra algorithms that access a matrix through QRAM, and classical dequantized algorithms with sampling and query access. At fixed condition number and accuracy, quantum algorithms use Õ(ρ) queries while the best dequantized algorithms use Õ(ρ⁴), where ρ is the normalized Frobenius norm. The authors construct worst-case dense linear systems showing this quartic gap is tight up to a logarithmic factor. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show the quartic gap between quantum and dequantized linear algebra algorithms is tight, via a lower bound covering many tasks.

entry.title: From Mixed to Pure: Understanding Quantum Phases via Canonical Purification
entry.summary: Lifting the mixed to the pure: quantum phases of matter from canonical purification arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies quantum phases of matter. Pure-state phases are defined through finite-depth local unitary connections, a notion recently extended to mixed states linked by locally reversible channels. The authors show that such a channel between mixed states can be lifted to a local isometry between their canonical purifications, so mixed states in the same phase have canonical purifications in the same pure-state phase. They give an explicit construction of the lifting isometry and illustrate the results with toric code under bit-flip noise and Chern insulator under fermion-number noise. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show locally reversible channels lift to local isometries between canonical purifications, with explicit Petz-based construction checked on toric code and Chern insulator examples.

entry.title: A quantum physics paper on how entanglement entropy scales in fractal dimensions
entry.summary: Scaling laws of entanglement entropy in fractal dimensions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how the entanglement entropy of free-fermion systems on fractal lattices, which have noninteger dimensions, scales with subsystem size. The authors derive upper and lower bounds set by the hopping across the subsystem boundary, and treat both pure states and mixed states from half-filled chiral zero modes. Under a uniform gap the entropy follows a boundary law, while an extensive zero-mode weight makes the mixed-state entropy follow the bulk dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive upper and lower bounds on free-fermion entanglement entropy scaling on fractal lattices, separating boundary-law and log-corrected cases, and analyzing zero-mode mixed-state entropy

entry.title: Device-independent multiparty key agreement using two-body correlations and balanced Dicke states
entry.summary: Device-independent conference key agreement from two-body correlators with balanced Dicke states arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how N≥4 (even) distant parties can agree on a shared secret key without detailed knowledge of their source or measurement devices. The authors show that two-body correlators alone, with balanced Dicke states, are sufficient for this device-independent conference key agreement. In the ideal setting, the certified key rate approaches 1−h[(N−2)/(4(N−1))], which tends to about 0.189 bits per round as N grows. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report two-body correlators suffice for device-independent conference key agreement, with a tight entropy bound keeping rates positive as N grows.

entry.title: Exponential quantum-classical query separations for cyclic Forrelation
entry.summary: Exponential quantum-classical query separations for cyclic Forrelation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the randomized classical query complexity of cyclic Forrelation, a cyclic version of k-Forrelation that asks for estimating a normalized trace built from k Boolean functions and Hadamard gates. For nonadaptive classical algorithms, it gives a nearly complete characterization, with tight bounds for even k and matching-order bounds up to a gap for odd k. It shows that k=3 admits a polylogarithmic-query classical algorithm, disproving a prior conjecture. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight nonadaptive classical query bounds for even k and refute a conjecture at k=3 using hidden-shift collision constructions.

entry.title: Efficient photonic GHZ measurements using only linear optics
entry.summary: High-efficiency photonic GHZ measurements with linear optics arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces a family of linear-optical GHZ measurements built on four-mode interferometers, showing that many-body interference makes photonic entangling operations more efficient. For four photons the success probability is 9/32, and adaptive variants project unsuccessful outcomes onto useful stabilizer states. The approach extends to larger GHZ measurements with exponentially higher success probability than previous linear-optical schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose linear-optical GHZ measurements using four-mode interferometers, reporting a 9/32 four-photon success probability and exponential gains for larger measurements.

entry.title: Unbounded gap between almost-quantum and commuting-operator correlations in zero-error communication
entry.summary: An Unbounded Separation of Almost-Quantum and Commuting-Operator Correlations in Zero-Error Communication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies a zero-error communication task in which Alice and Bob receive labels and Bob must decide whether the labels are equal, without ever erring but possibly abstaining. For every quantum model, the optimal probability of a conclusive answer is exactly 1/N, matching shared randomness. Almost-quantum correlations reach a success probability approaching 1/17, showing an unbounded separation from quantum correlations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that almost-quantum correlations are unboundedly stronger than quantum ones in zero-error equality communication, with closed-form SDP solutions across N and n-bit tasks.

entry.title: Almost-quantum correlations break information causality
entry.summary: Almost-Quantum Correlations Violate Information Causality arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether information causality, the principle that m classical bits cannot give a receiver more than m bits about the sender's independent data, holds for almost-quantum correlations. The authors show that these correlations violate information causality without bound. The violation is driven by zero-error certificates, which are rare but never wrong. The paper concludes that either information causality is a valid physical principle excluding these correlations, or no mutual information satisfying consistency, data processing, and the chain rule exists for theories realizing them. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show that almost-quantum correlations violate information causality without bound, using zero-error certificates, and discuss consequences for mutual information properties.

entry.title: Quantum query cost of checking whether a linear system is stable
entry.summary: Quantum query complexity of Hurwitz stability testing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how many quantum queries are needed to decide whether a matrix is Hurwitz stable, meaning all trajectories of the linear system converge to zero, given an exact block-encoding of the matrix. The complexity depends on the dimension n and a lower bound ν on the imaginary-axis distance. A lower bound of Ω(√n/ν) is proven even for real diagonal matrices. For Hermitian or normal matrices, an upper bound of O(√n ν⁻¹ log n) is given, matching the lower bound up to a logarithmic factor, while the general non-normal case has a weaker upper bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a quantum query lower bound Ω(√n/ν) for Hurwitz testing and an upper bound matching it up to a log factor for normal matrices, via projector block-encoding.

entry.title: Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate to a later-chosen recipient
entry.summary: Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate with a deferred recipient arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper shows how the ability to apply a two-qudit entangling gate can be secret-shared among several candidate nodes in advance. A provider encrypts half of a Bell pair into one share per node, and after a later key release only the selected node can complete an exact non-local CSUM^k gate with the user's data. The authors state that any coalition smaller than the number of candidates, or the key register alone, holds no information.

entry.title: Weighted hypergraph quantum states as resources for quantum sensing
entry.summary: Weighted hypergraph states as a resource for quantum metrology arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies weighted hypergraph states, a family of multi-qubit quantum states, and identifies subclasses defined by their graph topology that perform better in quantum metrology. Using quantum Fisher information and a new Dicke-basis representation, the authors show these subclasses outperform separable states and standard weighted graph states over broad ranges of edge weights. Analytical formulas for any number of qubits are provided, with a detailed analysis for four qubits. The authors also find that adding higher-order hyperedges can keep a quantum advantage under higher local dephasing noise.

entry.title: Topologically protected edge states in a single superconducting flux qubit
entry.summary: Topologically Protected Edge States in a Single Flux Qubit arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper shows that topological edge states can be realized in a simple superconducting circuit built from one inductively shunted flux qubit. The circuit's low-energy dynamics map analytically onto an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain, and numerical simulations of the full circuit confirm this mapping. Near a chiral point in parameter space, the edge states are numerically found to be topologically protected against chiral-symmetry-preserving perturbations such as charge noise. The authors conclude that protection effects previously associated with multi-qubit systems can also occur in a single qubit.

entry.title: Charge pumping and leptogenesis analogy in a symmetric mass generation phase on a four-leg ladder
entry.summary: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper uses density-matrix renormalization group simulations on a four-leg ladder to study a chiral fermion lattice model (the 3-4-5-0 model) with six-fermion interactions at one edge. Charge pumping stays quantized across weak, intermediate, and strong coupling, though the spatial distribution of pumped charge differs between boundary phases. At intermediate coupling the edge becomes fully gapped through symmetric mass generation. The authors also draw an analogy to a topological leptogenesis scenario in the Standard Model.

entry.title: Comparing photon sources for secure quantum key sharing without trusting detectors
entry.summary: Benchmarking Single-Photon Sources for Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper compares two single-photon source types for measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution: weak coherent pulses and quantum dot sources. Using decoy-state analysis, the authors find that quantum dot implementations outperform the best-case weak coherent pulse setup across all transmission distances, even at moderate mean photon numbers. They also show that both source types are highly sensitive to imperfect photon indistinguishability, which significantly affects key rates and maximum transmission distance.

entry.title: Comparing quantum and classical kernel methods for classification under controlled protocols
entry.summary: Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Classification: A Comparative Study with Classical Kernels arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper compares quantum kernel methods with classical kernels for classification under a protocol-controlled setup. It tunes the quantum bandwidth on the same grid budget as the classical kernel, recomputes kernels within each fold, and counts cost in hardware circuit evaluations. Across a 324-cell factorial design and four standard datasets, feature-map bandwidth tuning matters more than any quantum-classical difference. Tuned quantum kernels are statistically indistinguishable from a tuned RBF kernel on all four real datasets.

entry.title: Logical Bell inequalities for marginal Wigner negativity
entry.summary: Logical Bell Inequalities for Marginal Wigner Negativity arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper constructs logical Bell inequalities whose violations are determined by the Wigner function of a reduced quantum state. For odd-prime qudits, each phase-space point of a nonempty proper subsystem defines an inequality that is violated when its Gross Wigner value is negative. The normalized violation gives a lower bound on the contextual fraction in the complete Weyl measurement scenario, valid for any joint state with that marginal. A family of product states that saturates this bound is also identified.

entry.title: A resource-efficient quantum method that splits molecules into fragments and runs them in parallel on virtual QPU regions
entry.summary: Resource efficient Sample Based Quantum Simulation through Fragmentation and Virtual Partitioning of QPU arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces FMO-QVM-HCI-HSQD, a framework that splits a large molecular problem into fragments, runs them in parallel on virtual regions of a quantum processor, and uses a half-qubit circuit to reduce circuit depth. It was tested on IBM hardware with the water trimer and the carmofur_Mpro complex using up to 52 qubits. The results show lower two-qubit depth, reduced QPU time, and access to a much smaller determinant subspace than comparison methods, while keeping energies accurate.

entry.title: Solvable coupled cluster states in infinite dimensions with prescribed momentum distributions
entry.summary: Solvable coupled cluster states in d=∞ with prescribed momentum distribution arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper connects the coupled cluster wave function method with dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). In the infinite-dimensional limit of the hypercubic lattice, static expectation values of coupled cluster states can be evaluated in exact closed form. The authors show that any momentum distribution can be realized as the exact unique ground state of an explicit parent Hamiltonian, and that these states fail in the strong-coupling regime near the Mott transition, revealing a limitation of coupled cluster doubles.

entry.title: No generalised contextuality arises from the vacuum
entry.summary: No generalised contextuality from the vacuum arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper shows that, under certain conditions, generalised contextuality in the sense introduced by Spekkens cannot be created from the vacuum of a quantum field. Initially noncontextual qudit states do not become contextual merely by interacting with a quantum field. The authors verify this in two scenarios: a perturbative approach expanding the time evolution operator in powers of the coupling constant, and the limit of zero energy gap in the spectrum of the free detector Hamiltonian.

entry.title: GENIE: Learned quantum circuits as embedding solvers and when they work
entry.summary: GENIE: learned quantum circuits as embedding impurity solvers, and why compactness, not correlation strength, decides when they work arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces GENIE, an impurity solver for density matrix embedding theory in which a generative transformer learns the sampling circuit, trained on the quantum-selected configuration interaction energy. On N2, hydrogen chains, water and a hydrogen ring, it compares GENIE at equal determinant budget with classical selected CI methods and with sample-based quantum diagonalization. GENIE does not beat the best classical selection, and its failures are governed by wavefunction compactness relative to the budget rather than correlation strength. A cheap coupled-cluster-based estimate of compactness works as a router that predicts when GENIE should be used.

entry.title: Locality, Probability and the Relevance of History: A theory paper on how quantum nonlocality relates to relativity
entry.summary: Locality, Probability and the Relevance of History arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes a generalization of relativity's causal constraint to probabilistic theories: the probability of an event should be functionally determined by the probabilities of event occurrences in its immediate causal past. The author argues this differs from Bell's criterion of local causality and implies it only under an extra assumption that history is irrelevant. Consequently, Bell-inequality-violating quantum phenomena need not conflict with relativity, locality, statistical independence, or realism; they instead show that history is relevant.

entry.title: Focusing light through two coupled multimode fibers to build compact single-atom tweezer arrays
entry.summary: Focusing through coupled multimode fibers for miniaturized single-atom tweezer arrays arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper uses a 2x1 multimode fiber fused coupler to create two independent control channels sharing one output facet. Each channel forms near-diffraction-limited optical tweezers, and a small frequency offset between the channels suppresses interference. The tweezer separation is shown to be insensitive to misalignment of the input coupling.

entry.title: Electron-nuclear coupling in chemical and physical processes: how it matters when Born-Oppenheimer approximations break down.
entry.summary: The Role of Electron-Nuclear Coupling on Chemical and Physical Processes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper reviews the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) and Born-Oppenheimer-Huang (BOH) approaches to electron-nuclear motion, which are foundational for studying chemical and physical processes. It notes that the BO approximation often fails when excited electronic states are involved, because of coupling between states. The authors describe adiabatic potential energy surfaces and nonadiabatic coupling terms, which govern nuclear forces. Near conical intersections, these coupling terms can break molecular symmetry and qualitatively change observed behavior.

entry.title: Control-noise trade-offs in industrial silicon spin qubits
entry.summary: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ²⁸Si/SiGe Spin-1/2 Qubits arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies electron spin-1/2 qubits in 28Si/SiGe fabricated with Intel's 300 mm process and compares them with a reference device from RIKEN. The Intel devices reach π/2-gate fidelities at the 99.99% level and show longer idle coherence. The authors link micromagnet placement, set by the vertical stack design, to magnetic-field gradients that affect charge-noise conversion and drive efficiency, revealing a trade-off between integration layout and gate performance.

entry.title: Hybrid quantum models for trade surveillance: comparing quantum and classical classifiers for detecting pump-and-dump schemes
entry.summary: Hybrid Quantum Algorithms for Trade Surveillance Analytics arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper benchmarks four quantum and hybrid classifiers against classical baselines on a synthetic pump-and-dump detection task, using a shared split of 1,000 accounts and two 20-feature representations. The best model is classical XGBoost on ANOVA features, with a suspicious-class F1 of 61.4%. The hybrid quantum neural network reaches 54.5-57.9% F1 on an ideal simulator and 55.4-59.8% on ibm_fez hardware, outperforming six of eight classical configurations. The authors observe no quantum advantage.

entry.title: Channel dichotomies: interconverting channels under non-signalling superchannels
entry.summary: Channel dichotomies arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how quantum channels can be converted into one another using non-signalling superchannels, with the asymptotic conversion rate given by the ratio of channel capacities. The main result gives the second-order expansion of the optimal target length, where the coefficient is an inverse sesquinormal distribution determined by the capacities and dispersions. The authors extend state dichotomy theory to channels and note that this characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols.

entry.title: Designed classification tasks on noisy quantum processors that favor quantum over classical methods
entry.summary: Engineered Learning Problems on Noisy Quantum Processors arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper uses a projected quantum kernel on an engineered classification problem with 15, 30, and 45 qubits and reports a significant performance gap over classical methods. The results are reproduced across different quantum processors. The authors also show that error mitigation widens this gap by improving hardware performance and increasing classical difficulty, though the problem is artificial.

entry.title: Quantum Monte Carlo for Sovereign Debt Risk: A Proof of Concept
entry.summary: Toward Quantum Monte Carlo for Sovereign Debt Risk: A proof of concept arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a proof-of-concept pipeline using quantum amplitude estimation to compute the probability that a sovereign debt-to-GDP ratio exceeds a critical threshold at a given horizon. The pipeline combines a linearized two-factor Gaussian debt model, quantum state preparation on a 32 x 32 grid, a weighted-adder circuit, an integer comparator, and Maximum Likelihood Amplitude Estimation. On a noiseless simulator, the circuit estimate agrees with the exact target amplitude, with errors consistent with amplitude-estimation scaling. The authors stress that the model is deliberately simple, so the contribution is a demonstration of the encoding and estimation workflow rather than a practical advantage over classical methods.

entry.title: Fixing a Representation Limit in Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks
entry.summary: Overcoming the Representational Limitations of Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies amplitude encoding in quantum neural networks, showing that normalization makes it blind to nonzero real rescaling of inputs. The authors introduce a fixed nonlinear feature map that distinguishes all real inputs under amplitude encoding, adding no trainable parameters and keeping logarithmic qubit scaling. On three canonical classification benchmarks and a nonlinear synthetic dataset, the proposed encoding improves accuracy over conventional amplitude and angle encoding by 21 to 44 percent.

entry.title: Estimating fidelity bounds for non-stabilizer quantum states using local measurements
entry.summary: Bounding Fidelity of Non-Stabilizer States from Local Pauli Measurements arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies nonstabilizer states, often called magic, which are needed for universal quantum computation, and proposes a method to bound their fidelity. The approach selects operators with low measurement cost that share permutational symmetry and estimates them with parallel local Pauli measurements. The optimization reduces to a linear program with only O(n) variables, and nonlinear quantities such as purity can be handled with convex quadratic programs. Tests on hypergraph states with up to 500 qubits show substantially lower measurement overhead under local and global depolarizing noise.

entry.title: Query-efficient quantum multi-objective optimization for materials search using Bayesian weight selection
entry.summary: Query-Efficient Quantum Multi-Objective Optimization for Materials Configuration Search via Bayesian Weight Selection arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper addresses materials design as a multi-objective problem and proposes BW-QAMOO, which chooses each objective-weight vector for a quantum solver using Bayesian optimization rather than random sampling. On a frustrated alloy-configuration benchmark, it reaches the same Pareto hypervolume with a median 33% fewer scalarized solves than random-sampling QAMOO and 60–74% fewer than a uniform-grid baseline. A paired Wilcoxon test indicates the saving is significant, and the gain grows with the number of objectives.

entry.title: Chiral torsional double wells: how quantum tunneling and transition polarizability relate in small peroxide-type molecules
entry.summary: Chiral Torsional Double Wells: Tunneling and Polarizability arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies quantum tunneling between mirror-related wells of the torsional potential in hydrogen peroxide, hydrogen disulfide, and hydrogen diselenide, along with the polarizability matrix elements between their torsional states. The authors compute torsional states from relaxed CCSD(T)//MP2 potentials and a kinetic model without overall rotation. They find that tunneling slows sharply across the series while the matrix element grows, so slower coherent interconversion does not necessarily weaken the intrinsic transition polarizability.

entry.title: Using quantum measurement randomness to make diffusion models need fewer shots
entry.summary: Leveraging Quantum Measurement Randomness for Shot-Efficient Diffusion Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper treats the sampling noise from quantum measurements as a resource rather than a cost, using it in place of part of the randomness a diffusion sampler normally injects. The measurement error is modeled as multinomial noise passed through a trainable linear readout, and the diffusion process is formulated on a bounded zero-sum hyperplane mapped to the probability simplex. On an eight-dimensional Gaussian mixture, the method reaches comparable generation quality with 303 shots per sample against a high-shot reference of 1.6×10^6. Latent diffusion experiments on MNIST are also reported.

entry.title: A Highly Nondegenerate Photon-Pair Source for Detector-Matched QKD
entry.summary: A Highly Nondegenerate Photon-Pair Source for Detector-Matched Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a highly nondegenerate photon-pair source that needs a telecom-band single-photon detector on only one arm, with a silicon SPAD detecting the 548 nm photon at the source node. Two periodically poled KTP crystals pumped at 405 nm emit 548 nm and 1550 nm pairs, with the first unoptimised module producing about 1.5×10^6 pairs/s per mW. An asymptotic BBM92 model compares the cost per secret bit of its links against generic 2×1550 nm links. The source is also suited to clock synchronisation and detector calibration.

entry.title: Extending a quantum method for diagonalization to solving linear equations
entry.summary: Extending Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization to Systems of Linear Equations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper extends sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), originally developed for quantum chemistry, to solving linear systems Ax=b. The Hermitian matrix is decomposed in the Pauli basis, Trotterized time evolution of |b⟩ is sampled at several times to select computational-basis configurations, and the system is then solved classically by Galerkin projection onto the selected subspace. The authors prove the subspace solution is exact under a Krylov-support condition and optimal in the energy norm for symmetric positive-definite matrices, and report tests on IBM Quantum hardware along with the method's limitations.

entry.title: Solving hypergraph MAX-k-CUT with quantum computing
entry.summary: Solving the MAX-k-CUT problem for hypergraphs with quantum computing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the MAX-k-CUT problem on hypergraphs by representing them as spin systems with Ising interactions. The cost Hamiltonian is reduced to an Ising Hamiltonian with only pairwise interactions, which simplifies solving the problem on quantum computers. Using a 3-uniform tight-star hypergraph and a sunflower hypergraph as examples, the authors construct the Hamiltonians and present quantum protocols. MAX-3-CUT and MAX-4-CUT instances are evaluated with QAOA from p=2 to p=15 on IBM's Qiskit AerSimulator.

entry.title: Mathematical foundations of second quantization, introduced through spin-boson models
entry.summary: Mathematical foundations of second quantization: an introduction through spin-boson models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026These lecture notes present the mathematical foundations of second quantization, using spin-boson models (a two-level system coupled to a boson field) as the guiding example. They cover unbounded operators, single-mode boson fields, Fock spaces, and bosonic and fermionic creation and annihilation operators. The authors prove self-adjointness of these models and solve the pure dephasing and Jaynes-Cummings models explicitly. An appendix proves the rotating-wave approximation for the quantum Rabi model with an explicit error bound.

entry.title: Simulating decaying 2D vortices with a Carleman-Lattice Boltzmann method
entry.summary: Simulating two-Dimensional decaying vortex structure with the Carleman-Lattice-Boltzmann method arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper numerically studies the free decay of two-dimensional nonlinear vortex structures using the second-order-truncated Carleman-Lattice Boltzmann method (CLB2) on a 128×128 grid. At a Reynolds number of about 15, the method keeps amplitude errors below 10% over six diffusive times, while at about 46 errors grow beyond 10% with a modest effect on spatial structure. The authors suggest that closures or regularization could improve CLB2 accuracy without higher-order truncations.

entry.title: Quantum machine learning for seasonal geospatial time series using structured data encoding
entry.summary: Quantum machine learning geospatial time-series by seasonal encoding arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how data encoding affects quantum data reuploading models forecasting seasonal time series as circuit depth increases. The authors build fixed and adaptive seasonal encodings and test them on monthly precipitation from ERA5-Land for a semi-arid East African region, using a 14-month lag window and depths 1 to 6. Adaptive seasonal encodings preserve forecasting accuracy in ideal simulations and remain competitive with ARIMA, random forests, and LSTMs.

entry.title: Windowed Catodyne Measurements: Continuum vs. Exact Photon-Number Analysis
entry.summary: Windowed Catodyne Measurements: Continuum Approximation versus Exact Discrete Photon-Number Treatment arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies catodyne detection, where a Schrödinger cat state acts as the local oscillator, using only a finite window of the photon-sum variable. Continuum approximations suggest the window half-width works as a continuous control for coherence, but an exact discrete photon-number treatment shows that in the strong local-oscillator regime the window does not suppress coherence conditioned on the difference outcome. The authors also compute remote preparation of cat states with a finitely squeezed resource, finding high purity when the variable is resolved. The results identify when the continuum approximation can be trusted and when discrete photon-number structure is required.

entry.title: Quantum analogue of the Kolmogorov–Arnold representation theorem using Bernstein polynomials
entry.summary: Quantum Bernstein--Kolmogorov--Arnold approximation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the expressivity gap in quantum neural networks by establishing a quantum version of the classical Kolmogorov–Arnold representation theorem. It proposes a constructive approximation framework over fixed input coherent states, in which a single outer unitary evolution is dictated by the target function. The authors prove that the measurement probability reproduces the multidimensional Bernstein polynomial of the target, and that for any continuous multivariate function the joint quantum state converges uniformly to the target output register.

entry.title: Symmetries and model reduction in a cos2φ transmon qubit
entry.summary: Symmetries and model reduction in a cos 2ǎrphi transmon qubit arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a cos2φ transmon qubit, realized with a two-Cooper-pair interferometer, whose circuit contains three coupled modes. Using the separation of energy scales between the heavy transmon mode and the light internal modes, the authors derive an effective single-band Born-Oppenheimer model with a geometric correction and extend it to several bands. They identify the symmetries of the full and reduced Hamiltonians and derive exact selection rules.

entry.title: FaultScope: A software package for quickly pinpointing error sources in quantum error correction
entry.summary: FaultScope: A software package for fast error attribution in quantum error correction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents FaultScope, a classical simulator for quantum error correction circuits, written in Rust with a Python interface. It estimates logical error rates and their derivatives with respect to individual component error rates from the same sampled and decoded shots. This lets errors be attributed to specific noisy components, helping identify where targeted noise reduction would help most.

entry.title: A hybrid message-passing and electric-field method for machine-learned electrostatic QM/MM simulations
entry.summary: A Hybrid Message-Passing and Electric-Field Representation for Electrostatic QM/MM Embedding with Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses hybrid quantum/classical simulations, where a machine learning interatomic potential replaces the costly quantum calculation to extend simulation time. It shows that existing approaches using only external electric-field features cannot distinguish certain environments, limiting accuracy. The authors extend the equivariant TensorNet architecture by including nearby classical atoms in message passing and using electric-field features for more distant environment. They report that this combination is more accurate than either approach alone.

entry.title: eCAS: an orbital embedding method for quantum computers that splits a large molecule into smaller, independently solvable pieces.
entry.summary: eCAS: An Orbital Embedding Method for Quantum Computing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Future fault-tolerant quantum computers will still be limited in the size of systems they can handle, so embedding methods are needed. The paper introduces eCAS, an orbital embedding method that builds a multi-CAS problem whose localized active spaces can each be solved independently with any quantum algorithm. It uses Schmidt decomposition to construct initial impurity and bath orbitals and adds localized environment orbitals based on a mutual correlation criterion. The criterion allows systematic improvement without iteratively determined quantities.

entry.title: Quantum Popcorn: shape of a phase transition bubble
entry.summary: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble arXiv · Oct 30, 2026A quantum tunneling event is usually pictured as a spherical bubble of true vacuum appearing at rest. This paper argues that the bubble is spherical only at leading semiclassical order, while at the next order it is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce solution. Using the half-bounce path integral, the authors derive the field's wave functional on the nucleation slice and compute the root-mean-square quadrupole moment of the nucleated bubble. The relative deformation of the bubble wall radius scales as δR/R ~ (ħ/S_b)^{1/2}, where S_b is the bounce action.

entry.title: oracq: A framework for building and analyzing quantum algorithms for scientific computing
entry.summary: oracq: A Modular Framework for Implementing and Analyzing Quantum Scientific Computing Algorithms arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents oracq, a Python framework that treats the concrete realization of oracles in quantum scientific computing algorithms as a managed, checkable choice. Algorithms are stored as register-level programs with typed but unimplemented oracle slots, which can later be bound to different realizations such as gate networks, QRAM tables, or reversible arithmetic circuits and compared. Two end-to-end workflows are provided: a quantum finite-volume pipeline for the compressible Euler equations and a quantum homotopy-analysis pipeline for nonlinear PDEs. The framework is openly available on GitHub.

entry.title: Analytic level-spacing statistics of the quantum Rabi model
entry.summary: Analytic level statistics of the quantum Rabi model arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper derives an analytic expression for the distribution of energy-level spacings in the quantum Rabi model. At high energies, the spectrum in a fixed parity sector is a uniformly spaced ladder modulated by a decaying oscillation, whose alternating sign splits spacings into two branches. Counting how often these branches exceed a given spacing yields an analytic spacing density whose range and twin peaks match exact diagonalization histograms. The same analysis gives an expression for the ratio of consecutive spacings, which needs no unfolding and also agrees closely with numerical results.

entry.title: Real-time BP decoder for a high-rate quantum error correction code
entry.summary: Real-time BP decoding of a high-rate QEC code arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a real-time FPGA decoder for a high-rate [[512,174,8]] 3D product qLDPC code. The authors build a circuit-level detector-error model for a compact syndrome-extraction schedule and propose a small parallel ensemble of row-wise serial min-sum decoders with cumulative memory. The decoder is reported to match BP+OSD-CS10 accuracy with one core and Relay-BP accuracy with three cores.

entry.title: Quantum sensing using a helper qubit with low dressed-state leakage
entry.summary: Helper-assisted quantum sensing with low dressed-state leakage arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a two-qubit sensing protocol in which only a helper qubit is read out, with the signal encoded in its phase through calibrated loading and unloading. Leakage into a selected dressed-state band is kept small. Simulations in a driven open-system model with uncertain coupling and finite-duration resets show that finite measurement records still support estimation at the tested settings.

entry.title: Distilling Knowledge from Search: Decoder Model Factory for Quantum LDPC Codes
entry.summary: Distilling Knowledge from Search: Decoder Model Factory for Quantum LDPC Codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces GraphMP, a learning-based message-passing decoder for quantum LDPC codes that transfers across code families, sizes, error rates, and noise models without fine-tuning. Model-guided beam search refines candidate error patterns, trading extra decoding time for lower logical error rates. The authors propose a decoder model factory that trains successive models on experience generated by earlier models and distills verified search trajectories into reusable training data.

entry.title: Loss-aware optimization of realistic GKP state preparation
entry.summary: Loss-aware optimization of realistic GKP gid states arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses how photon loss affects the practical preparation of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, which are leading candidates for bosonic quantum computation. The authors propose a loss-aware optimization procedure that uses GKP squeezing as the figure of merit, built on a ground-state representation of GKP states. Numerical simulations for square, hexagonal, and asymmetric GKP states show that optimal preparation generally uses a different initial grid spacing than the ideal code state, and the optimized states show better squeezing and greater resilience to loss.

entry.title: Reusing light sources over time to prepare GKP quantum states more efficiently
entry.summary: Time-Domain Multiplexing for Resource-Efficient Heralded GKP State Preparation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how to prepare Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) quantum states with fewer squeezed light sources and less demanding photon detectors, using time-domain multiplexing. The authors simulate circuits that reuse one or two squeezed sources with an end-to-end differentiable Bargmann framework. Some nine-mode configurations keep fidelities above 0.95 with one heralded photon per measured mode, and two-mode multiplexing keeps fidelities near 0.80 at 1.0 dB loss per channel.

entry.title: PyQLAS: A Library for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Linear System Solving
entry.summary: PyQLAS: A Quantum-Classical Hybrid Solver Library for Linear Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents PyQLAS, a library that combines quantum and classical computation to solve linear systems. It builds three nested solvers around one variational core, keeping the quantum circuit width fixed while the classical host handles problem growth. The same interface runs on a state-vector simulator, a local sampler, and a real superconducting processor. The library is validated on IEEE 118-bus power flow, where it converges to the specified tolerance and matches the classical reference solution closely.

entry.title: Proof that the Petz-Fuchs smoothed quantum state is optimal
entry.summary: Optimality of the Petz-Fuchs Smoothed State arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Quantum state smoothing estimates the state of an open quantum system by combining past and future measurement records. This paper proves that the Petz-Fuchs smoothed state, derived from quantum retrodiction, majorizes all other smoothed states that depend only on the filtered state and the retrofiltered effect. The author characterizes the full set of smoothed states satisfying this condition to establish the result.

entry.title: Estimating a Quantum Correlation Measure from Measurements
entry.summary: Estimation of Quantum Umlaut Information arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces measured quantum umlaut information, which replaces Umegaki relative entropy with measured relative entropy so that correlations can be estimated from measurement statistics without full state descriptions. The authors build a quantum generative adversarial framework that optimizes reference states and measurements for unknown bipartite states and classical-quantum channels. They derive a state-dependent gap bound relating this measure to the original quantity. Numerical simulations show the trained estimates are close on average to independently computed references.

entry.title: Parametric Boost of an Optical Spring in a Dark-Port Cavity
entry.summary: Parametric Enhancement of an Optical Spring in a Dark Signal-Recycling Cavity arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper experimentally places an optical parametric amplifier inside a cavity at the dark port of a Michelson interferometer.
